hypotheses.content: Predicted local extrema remain useful acquisition signals, but their survival is scaffold- and endpoint-dependent. Latest measurements removed several proposed strong-region features, including the large m71 completion decline and m132 completion maximum. Measured decreases on m155 and upper-loading m127 show that imposing monotonicity would also discard real catalog responses. Remaining features require matched neighboring labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected boundary comparisons can repair misplaced curvature while preserving genuine exceptions. Testing different graph environments limits propagation of a correction from a single surprising label.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which remaining m5, m130, m48 and phenolic-aldehyde features survive measurement, and does the observed upper-loading m127 completion decrease persist at lower loading?

hypotheses.content: The proposed loading-independent m33 onset decline from 20/1 to 50/1 is weakened. It occurs at the loading extremes, but midpoint onset increased from 7.77 to 8.49 mL. Midpoint completion increased from 21.69 to 38.59 mL, close to upper-loading 39.01 mL and substantially above lower-loading 26.73 mL. A linear completion-loading relationship is therefore also insufficiently supported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs separate endpoint responses and nonlinear loading interactions. A shared onset correction or interpolation between the loading extremes would miss the measured midpoint behavior.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does midpoint 10/1 connect smoothly to its measured increasing 20/1–50/1 endpoints, or reveal additional curvature before that segment? This test constrains the earlier curve but cannot establish repeatability at 50/1.

hypotheses.content: Broad transfer of the late, compact lower-loading m124 pure-EA record across m124 loadings and related fused aromatic graphs is rejected. Both other m124 loadings and the tested m215 and m7 pure-EA rows had ordinary early onsets. The exceptional lower-loading m124 record remains measured evidence with unresolved loading specificity or variability; its cause is not established.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The last retraining propagated an exceptional onset correction beyond its measured scope. Negative transfer can affect many rows even when a newly acquired label is locally informative.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can any independent identical-protocol measurement reproduce the lower-loading m124 boundary response? Other fused-graph boundary experiments test remaining response shapes, not the mechanism of that exceptional record.

hypotheses.content: Several measured loading contrasts have much larger onset changes than completion changes, including m51 at 10/1, m90 at 5/1, and m135 at 5/1. These are associations within recorded protocols, not proof of a common overload mechanism. Their transfer across solvent strength and functional-group environments remains conditional.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Nearly loading-insensitive predictions can retain substantial V1 errors after V2 has become accurate. Matched loading experiments can teach endpoint-specific sensitivity rather than a common shift of the elution interval.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m90's missing 5/1 midpoint preserve onset ordering, and does m135 loading sensitivity appear already at 2/1 and persist at 10/1? Do the m39 and m44 comparisons show different endpoint sensitivities?

hypotheses.content: Dicarbonyl-containing rows require different condition-response scales. Measured m80 and m81 weak-condition completions can be modest, whereas m82 and m78 show large weak-solvent growth. The two measured midpoint m81 20/1 completions also differ substantially. Structural environment is a plausible contributor, but loading protocol and variability prevent a simple causal or dicarbonyl-wide correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A connected comparison of shallow and steep curves can establish boundaries for transfer among related carbonyl graphs. Multiple m81 labels test whether its shallow response generalizes across loading instead of fitting one variable midpoint record.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do lower-loading m81 5/1–10/1–50/1 and upper-loading 10/1 retain modest completion volumes, while upper-loading m82 10/1–20/1 preserves its steep transition?

hypotheses.content: The current predictor places a very compact weak-solvent segment on m147 around 10/1–20/1 and a shallow completion minimum on m62 around 10/1. These are untested model features. Either endpoint could be biased, and a compact predicted interval alone provides no evidence that the corresponding measured response will be compact.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Short-retention rows are an important part of the Row-distribution. Testing their endpoint geometry can improve ordinary V1/V2 accuracy and avoid allowing rare compact records to distort nearby response curves.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched m147 and m62 10/1–20/1 labels confirm interval contraction or expose V1/V2 bias, and does the nearby m148 graph retain its predicted wider interval?

feedback_interpretation: The latest results strongly weaken propagation from exceptional compact records. m124 pure EA measured 4.21/9.90 and 4.55/9.97 mL at the two higher loadings, producing acquisition-time onset overpredictions of 13.21 and 12.71 mL. Tested m215 and m7 pure-EA onsets were also early. Likewise, upper-loading m209 at 2/1 measured 5.89/11.18 mL, unlike the midpoint 21.85/21.90 mL record; midpoint pure EA and 1/1 were ordinary. These outcomes reject broad loading transfer of those features without explaining or discarding the exceptional records. I therefore test remaining boundary shapes with direct controls rather than extending a late-onset correction across families. m33 also changed the interpretation: its midpoint onset increased from 20/1 to 50/1, while completion rose to 38.59 mL, close to the upper-loading result. This weakens both a shared onset-decline account and simple interpolation of completion between loading extremes. The m51 and m90 lower-loading results exposed substantial onset underprediction with much smaller completion errors, strengthening the priority of endpoint-specific loading comparisons. The m60 midpoint result was comparatively close, supporting selective testing rather than an alcohol-wide correction. m6 measured a shallow completion rise through 10/1–20/1–50/1, and m113 and m121 weak-condition results were mostly close to prediction; I reduce further dense ether sampling. Several strong-region features disappeared: m71's large predicted completion decline, m132's completion maximum, m27's proposed 1/1-to-2/1 completion decline, and m87's onset decline. However, existing m155 and m127 measurements retain decreases, so monotonicity remains a prior rather than a rule. All errors discussed here are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The 32 labels form connected comparisons with measured anchors. Loading experiments address recent V1 failures while testing where those corrections stop transferring across solvent strength or chemical environment. The m81 and m82 segments distinguish shallow and steep carbonyl responses and examine loading scope without assuming that a functional-group count determines retention. Strong-boundary experiments test remaining predicted features on fused aromatics, nitriles, phenolic aldehydes, methoxy ketones and the O–Cl environment; matched controls help prevent another isolated-label correction from spreading broadly. The m147/m148 and boronate experiments cover short-retention responses whose endpoint geometry remains underanchored. These roles target predictive generalization across the Row-distribution rather than favorable chromatography or maximal retention. Multiple selections on one molecule discriminate curve shape or loading response; identical-condition candidate copies are not selected together. Cross-molecule comparisons retain their recorded loading-solvent and volume differences, and missing experimental factors remain possible explanations for variable observations. Loading amount is density times sample volume. Quantile spans and CW distances are supporting model summaries, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 is the elution interval width. These 32 IDs and their exact associated premeasurement predictions in this packet are frozen together before any new label reveal.
